summary: Not covered: repo has greedy covers of residue rings Z/L (EXPONENT_COVERING.md §4) and fixed-menu barriers (HARDNESS_MAP.md:230, B1) but no menu-size-vs-X law. Ran exact lazy-greedy set cover (C, scripts/z52d_audit_A0_setcover.c) of primes p ≡ 1 (24) in [X,2X) by (★) items (u,C) [(4uC−1) | p+u], X = 10^4..10^8: greedy menu = 33, 110, 330, 940, 2484 (targets 124…664109; uncoverable = (★) failures 0,1,3,0,0), local log-log slope in X 0.52, 0.48, 0.46, 0.42 (≈ 3·√#targets); 90 % coverage needs 21, 34, 43, 46, 46 items (plateau = fixed-menu density), 99 % needs 32, 100, 243, 422, 516, and 28–39 % of greedy picks are singletons with m up to ~2X. EVIDENCE: menu growth is power-like and driven entirely by the tail — the quantitative face of B1 (a fixed menu covers a fixed ~90 % density); calibration only, no proof lead.

summary: Not in repo (no quasirandom-group/Nikolov–Pyber discussion; Gowers only as Gowers norms, BRAINSTORM/wildcard_list.md W7). Did the step for primes q < 50 (scripts/z52d_audit_A0_gowers.py): any integer letter range reduces mod q to at most q letters S(a) = [[a,−1],[1,0]], so |A||B||C| ≤ q³ while Gowers/Nikolov–Pyber need > |G|³/m ≈ 2q⁸ — fails by a factor ~q⁵ for every q (ratio 2e−3 at q=3 down to 2e−9 at q=47); letter sets are 1-parameter curves of density q⁻², never dense. Directly: S(a)S(b)S(c) = [[(ab−1)c−a, 1−ab],[bc−1, −b]] covers all of SL₂(F_q) except exactly q(q−2) elements (lower-right 0, not upper-right −1; verified), and every trace occurs, so the local mod-q layer of length-3 words is trivially (almost) surjective by elementary algebra — consistent with the known absence of local obstructions (BL) and irrelevant to the global/2-adic ES₅ condition.
next: None; the criterion is structurally inapplicable (letter sets are 1-dimensional in a 3-dimensional group).

summary: Covered by CONDITIONAL_ES.md Prop 2.3 + Rem 2.4 (= FRONTIER §3 B3): every encoding with fibres ≤ p^{o(1)} has main term ≤ 2μ(p)f(p), f(p) the total solution count (polylog on average, ET Thm 1.1). Writing it out shows the item's premise is moot rather than merely confirmed: the solution set is finite, so huge ranges are empty — in (★) C = (p+u+B)/(4uB) ≤ (p+2)/4, and in the divisor form d·d′ = 4Cp+1 with d ≡ d′ ≡ −1 (mod 4C) forces (4C−1)² ≤ 4Cp+1, i.e. C ≲ p/4 (finite trial set |𝓡| = (p/4)log p, PARITY_AUDIT Lemma 2.1); Type I/e-slice parameters are likewise bounded (4/p has finitely many solutions). So 'C up to p^A' adds nothing past A = 1, and the heuristic Σ_{C≤p^A} log(Cp)/C ≈ A log²p overcounts. Also the item's Type I estimate log p·log²X at X = p gives log³p, which is the all-n average, not the prime average log²p (ET).

Repo treats sum-product only qualitatively (FORCED_WINDOW.md:263–266 'no step where sum–product enters'; BRAINSTORM/gon_incidence_kloosterman.md (c3) → B4); energies never measured. Computed (scripts/z52d_audit_A0_energy.py) E×(divisor classes of N_e mod e)/E_rand for e ≤ 1000, e ≡ 3 (4), 400 primes p ≡ 1 (24) in [10⁶, 3·10⁶] + 150 composites: prime-level mean log-ratio is flat — 40 hardest primes (14–19 of 250 successful slices) 0.515, typical 0.507, composites 0.494. Slice-level: failing slices have higher energy (+0.39 in log stratified by k, but only +0.16 once stratified by (k, e-range)), and 28 % of failing slices are exact subgroup traps (−1 ∉ ⟨classes⟩, the known character obstruction), so the signal is the known trapping mechanism plus an e-confound, not an additive-progression effect. EVIDENCE, null for the item's hypothesis.
next: None; energy across consecutive windows does not separate hard primes at 10⁶.

summary: Read erdosproblems.com/308: smallest integer not a sum of distinct 1/n, n ≤ N (Croot [Cr99]: H_N − (9/2)(1+o(1))(log log N)²/log N ≤ f(N) ≤ H_N − (1/2)(1+o(1))(log log N)²/log N, so the representable integers are {1..⌊H_N⌋} or {1..⌊H_N⌋−1}) — a statement about integers as sums of ~N^{1−o(1)} unit fractions, not 3-term representations of 4/p. The repo already treats the Croot/Bloom machinery (BRAINSTORM/addcomb_unit_fraction_density.md, O142(c); B2_ACROSS_FIELDS.md:61): §3.1 term-count (|S| ≥ N^{1−o(1)}), §3.3 count scale (B3), and §3.2 shows that 'fix one denominator, complete with two terms' at k = 3 is exactly the ET Type I/II divisor parametrisation. Problem 308 itself is not cited in the repo, but nothing in it changes that verdict.

Covered by BRAINSTORM/nonab_homogeneous_dynamics.md (O147(b)) §1 (H3) + §3 Lemma B (EMM/Oppenheim counts cannot see a polylog fibre; need ε < 1/(nxyz)) and BRAINSTORM/z52_deep_thin_pointwise_opus.md:81,153. Doing the step adds a sharper reason: Oppenheim/LMMS concern forms NOT proportional to rational ones, while Q = xy+yz+zx has integer coefficients, so Q(ℤ³) ⊂ ℤ and 'effective density of values' is vacuous; the rational-form substitute (counting integer points on level sets Q = m, Duke–Rudnick–Sarnak/Eskin–McMullen) counts over growing regions (B3/B6), and the ES locus Q = (4/n)xyz is a cubic, not a quadric level set. Checked arXiv:1904.00290 abstract: it is the effective avoidance principle for unipotent orbits near ℚ-subvarieties (J. Anal. Math. 2023), a tool toward quantitative density, not itself an ES-usable count.

No disagreement-guided analysis in the repo, but its ingredients are: two (★) models M_BM (BM_CORRECTED_COUNT) and M_BM·F (RESIDUE_HARDNESS §2.3, scripts/z52c_rh_hard.py). Recomputed R, M₀, M_BM for all 39 095 primes p ≡ 1 (4) in (10³, 10⁶] (scripts/z38_mbm.c) and compared the 5 % tails of log F (balanced, 1955 primes each; scripts/z52d_audit_A0_disagree.py): on the mean the class-factor model wins decisively in both tails (bias of log((R+1)/(M+1)): M_BM −0.32 / +0.54, M_BM·F +0.09 / +0.11; middle 20 %: all models equal). The low-F tail holds 5 of the 7 (★) zeros, but swap-Poisson P(0)=e^{−M/2} predicts 2.3 (M_BM) vs 13.6 (M_BM·F) there — the mean model is right, the zero law at reduced mean is too pessimistic by ≈2.7×. This sharpens but matches RESIDUE_HARDNESS §0 item 6 ('zero law mixed', failures in low-F classes); no new mechanism.
